r: Kings were **Vedic**; **royal women** were the main patrons of Buddhism at Nagarjunakonda, giving **without male intervention**, while the men patronised Hindu cults
Gifts by the Ikshvaku family both to **Hindu temples** and to **Buddhist monks**
Sister of Santamula; **paternal aunt** of Virapurushadatta
**First woman donor**; rebuilt the **Maha Chaitya** in Virapurushadatta's **6th** regnal year; **9 ayaka pillars**; **170 dinari-masakas**
Pillar for **her mother** at the Aparamahavinaseliya chaitya; daughter Chathasri also gave
Sinhala Vihara; viharas for foreign monks; ranked **first among women donors**
Mostly **Prakrit ayaka-pillar** records of Virapurushadatta's 6th regnal year; each names the donor by her tie to the king
Ikshvakus were the **first to date** records by **year, month and day**
Tried to make the **intelligentsia partners in agricultural development** – gave **gold, cows, ploughs and land**; brought **Brahmins from the north** and gave them **agraharas**
Grants of land and its royal income, mostly to **Brahmins**
Administration + army; temples + festivals; poets + scholars; gifts to religious bodies – some also on **tanks and canals**
From the Satavahana **trade economy** to an **agrarian, agrahara-based** early medieval order
Tax on industries, professions and trade
**Lower than under the Satavahanas**; **Roman gold and silver coins** at Nagarjunakonda and a **Roman-style amphitheatre** at **Vijayapuri**
Of **lead and copper**; symbols **Ujjain symbol, elephant, lion**; found in Guntur, Krishna and Godavari districts
Rose through **Brahmadeya** grants (exempt from **18 taxes**) – a new **landlord class**
With the **Kshatrapas of Ujjain** and the **Chutus** (Kodabalisri married Vishnurudra Sivalananda Satakarni)
**Matronymics** (Vasishthiputra, Mathariputra), naming after the **grandfather** (Ehuvala Santamula) and **sati** (Satisahagamanam)
